sentences.text:
Opposite Parties
 Mr. Shashanka Patra, A.S.C.
 Coram:
 Justice Chittaranjan Dash
 Order
Order No. 22.03.2023
01. 1.
Heard the learned counsel for the Petitioners and the State.

2. By means of this application, the Petitioners seek grant of bail U/s.438 Cr.P.C. in apprehension of arrest for their alleged involvement in the offences U/s.363/366/376(2)(n)/376(3)/294/ 323/34,
I.P.C. and Section 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012, in connection with Dasamanthpur P.S. Case No.136 of 2022 corresponding to G.R. Case No.1295 of 2022 pending in the court of the learned Addl. Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Jeypore.

3. Regard being had to the nature of the allegations against the present Petitioners, seriousness,
gravity of the offences and the facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that the offence under the POCSO Act is involved, while this Court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the Petitioners, the Petitioners is given liberty to surrender and move for bail before the learned Addl.
Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Jeypore in the aforesaid G.R. // 2 // Case No.1295 of 2022 within three weeks from today.

In the event of their surrender and motion for bail within the aforesaid period, learned Addl. Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Jeypore shall do well to dispose of the bail application of the petitioners on the same day on merit in accordance with law,
presuming it to be a direction in affirmative.

4. Case Diary be transmitted and made available to the learned courts below, at the cost of the Petitioners, as far as possible, to facilitate disposal of the bail application of the Petitioners on the same day, if there be no other legal impediment.
